captions.sub: A NEW RECORD ON ANOTHER WORLD
captions.say: Twenty-eight point one miles. That is how far one robot has now driven on another world, and it just made history.

captions.sub: Millions of miles from the nearest driver
captions.say: And here's the wild part. For most of that journey, no human was steering. The rover was making its own decisions.
This is NASA's Perseverance rover. Stay to the end, because one number in this story will really surprise you.
But first, meet the old champion. NASA's Opportunity rover began exploring Mars in two thousand four, and kept rolling until twenty eighteen.
In nearly fifteen years, Opportunity drove twenty-eight point oh six miles. Forty-five point one six kilometers. For years, nobody on another world had gone farther.
That record looked untouchable. Then came a newer, tougher rover, with a very different driving style.
Launched in twenty twenty, Perseverance touched down in Jezero Crater in February twenty twenty-one, a place that once held an ancient lake.

captions.sub: A rocket-powered sky crane lowers the rover on cables
captions.say: A rocket-powered sky crane lowered the car-sized rover to the surface on cables. Then it flew away, and the real journey began.
From that day on, every wheel turn counted.
Then came sol two thousand and six, a Martian day, which on Earth was October eleventh, twenty twenty-six.
Perseverance was driving toward an area called Idubi, near the western rim of Jezero Crater, when the numbers ticked closer to Opportunity's mark.
And then it happened. The odometer hit twenty-eight point one zero miles, forty-five point two two kilometers, eclipsing Opportunity's twenty-eight point oh six.

captions.sub: The same distance, almost three times faster
captions.say: And here's the kicker. Opportunity needed nearly fifteen years to cover that distance. Perseverance did it in just five and a half.

captions.text: SO HOW DID IT DO IT?
captions.say: So how did a rover go this far this fast? The secret is a built-in driver.
It's called AutoNav, a self-driving system. While rolling, the rover photographs the terrain and builds a three-D map of hazards.

captions.sub: Rocks, slopes and sand traps, all scored for danger
captions.say: Every glance measures about six hundred thousand points. Rocks, slopes, sand traps, all scored for danger before a single wheel turns.

captions.sub: Between waypoints chosen by planners on Earth
captions.say: Rover planners on Earth choose the waypoints. Between them, Perseverance plots its own course around every hazard it can see.
More than ninety percent of Perseverance's total distance was driven with AutoNav. On Opportunity, the first Martian AutoNav handled about five percent.

captions.text: WOULD YOU TRUST A ROBOT DRIVER?
captions.say: Quick question for you. Would you trust a robot driver on a planet with no roads? Tell us in the comments.
Here's the surprise I promised. NASA's original mission plan called for driving no more than twelve point four miles.

captions.sub: More than 2x the plan, and still going
captions.say: Perseverance has blown well past that. It has driven more than twice the planned distance, and it is still going.
Steven Lee, project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says all of the rover's mobility systems are fully operational, with favorable extended wear tests.
Here's the route, from the landing site in twenty twenty-one to the record-setting drive in twenty twenty-six.

captions.sub: Ancient river delta  |  route is illustrative
captions.say: It crossed the crater floor, climbed the ancient river delta, and then headed west, up toward the rim of the crater.

captions.sub: Some of the oldest terrain ever explored
captions.say: Its next target, Idubi, may hold some of the oldest terrain ever explored anywhere in the solar system.

captions.sub: One careful decision at a time
captions.say: Forty-five kilometers of Mars, one careful decision at a time.

captions.sub: Farthest distance driven on another world
captions.say: So where does that put Perseverance on the all-time leaderboard of off-world driving?

captions.sub: 45.22 km, ahead of Opportunity by only about 60 meters
captions.say: First place, Perseverance with forty-five point two two kilometers. Opportunity is right behind at forty-five point one six. A margin of only about sixty meters.

captions.text: THE MOON IS ON THE LIST
captions.say: Third place belongs to the Soviet moon rover Lunokhod Two, which covered thirty-nine kilometers back in nineteen seventy-three.
Curiosity, still exploring Mars, has driven thirty-eight point one five kilometers. And the Apollo seventeen lunar rover, driven by astronauts, covered thirty-five point seven four.
But this was never about breaking records. Perseverance is a geologist on wheels, hunting for signs of ancient life.
On this drive, it was exploring traces of ancient hydrothermal systems, places where hot water once flowed through rock.
At a location called Lac de Charmes, it even captured a self-portrait against a sweeping backdrop of ancient Martian terrain.
Mark Maimone, from the robotics team, says the newer software teaches the rover to steer less and roll more.

captions.sub: The team thinks it could more than double its distance
captions.say: And this record is far from the end. The mission team thinks Perseverance could eventually more than double the distance it has already driven.
With every mobility system working, NASA expects the rover to keep adding to this record for many years to come.

captions.sub: The milestone coincides with 30 years of NASA rovers on Mars
captions.say: The milestone also arrives as NASA marks three decades of rover operations on Mars.
That's the story of a robot that out-drove every machine before it. What should we explore next? Tell us in the comments.
